A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main texts, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: Section 8 reports original simulations comparing average versus discounted robust Nash-Iteration and robust versus non-robust Nash-Iteration.

after.justification: Appendix J retains those simulations and adds TD-descent experiments across 30 independently generated random games.

M1.justification: v4 retains Robust Nash-Iteration as Algorithm 2 and adds Robust TD Descent. Algorithms 1 and 3 introduce projected updates of policies and gain/bias variables on different timescales, using a smoothed TD complementarity objective with a feasibility penalty.

E1.justification: Appendix J.1 adds unstructured random games with rewards in [0,1] and interval transition uncertainty. This broadens the simulated environment population beyond v2's prosperous/deprived clusters with Gaussian rewards and KL uncertainty balls, which remain in J.2.

E2.justification: The retained comparisons use the same discounted robust Nash-Iteration and non-robust average-reward Nash-Iteration baselines. The new TD experiment evaluates no competing solver.

E3.justification: v4 adds a 600-iteration planning evaluation measuring global robust TD gap and robust Nash gap, with Bellman problems solved through relative value iteration. The retained experiments keep their reward metric, discount-factor range of 0.5–0.99 and KL radius of 0.01.

E4.justification: v4 Figure 1 adds a convergence diagnostic examining whether decreasing TD gap accompanies progress toward equilibrium, measured by Nash gap. The earlier worst-case robustness comparison is retained unchanged.

E5.justification: v2 displays individual random-environment curves without quantified uncertainty. v4 J.1 introduces mean curves and standard-deviation bands across 30 independent random games; it does not report increased repetitions for the retained experiments.

E6.justification: v4 Figure 1 adds results showing decreasing TD and Nash gaps over 600 iterations. The reward-result panels in v2 Figures 1–2 are identical to v4 Figures 2–3, so they establish no revised performance or ranking.

T1.justification: v4 adds TD complementarity, smoothing, Lipschitz and stationarity analyses. Assumption 5.1 introduces optimal-bias uniqueness, and Appendix E replaces v2's asserted unit bias bound with a Cspan argument. Bellman uniqueness proofs are expanded, and the counterexample's minimax value changes from epsilon to epsilon/(1+epsilon) in v2 Lemma B.1 versus v4 Lemma C.1.

C1.justification: The algorithmic contribution expands from Nash-Iteration with an equilibrium oracle to include an oracle-free TD method with a stationarity guarantee. The weakly communicating existence result now requires optimal-bias uniqueness. The central irreducible-equilibrium and discounted-approximation claims remain.

C2.justification: v4 corrects v2's discussion suggesting bias nonuniqueness under irreducibility. It explains the additional uniqueness requirement for weak communication and explicitly distinguishes TD stationarity from Nash equilibrium convergence in Remark 6.4. Section 8 adds substantive limitations concerning rectangular uncertainty, shared worst-case kernels and stronger local convergence guarantees.

D1.justification: Appendices H/J add gain/bias anchoring, projection constraints, step-size conditions and RVI-based evaluation details. Reproducibility remains limited: numerical smoothing, penalty and step-size choices are unspecified, and the experimental Bellman-solve description differs from the gradient updates in the pseudocode.

R1.justification: v4 distinguishes Shapley's zero-sum result from Fink's general-sum equilibrium result and adds positioning around equilibrium complexity, TD methods, Moreau smoothing and weak communication. The existing three related-work themes remain, with their discussion relocated to Appendix A.

P1.justification: Sections 3–6 and substantial portions of the proofs are rewritten with expanded explanations and revised terminology. Related work and experiments move to appendices, the algorithm section is reorganized, and limitations, acknowledgments and an impact statement are added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout with running headers. Nash-Iteration pseudocode and existing comparison figures move to appendices. A new two-panel TD figure and TD pseudocode displays are added.

improvement.justification: v4 improves assumption disclosure, corrects the minimax calculation and adds uncertainty reporting. However, its major TD extension has unresolved support gaps: Algorithms 1/3 update gains and biases by gradients, whereas J.1 uses optimal Bellman solutions. Theorem H.15 also infers full-sequence convergence from weighted summability without justifying that inference. These benefits and unresolved method/proof issues prevent a reliable judgment of the net overall quality change.
